brief.greeting: Good morning. Kernel rc4 landed, and a USB GPU fits on a stick.

stories.headline: Linux 7.4‑rc4 lands with driver focus
stories.body: **Patch drop, half drivers:** Linux kernel 7.4‑rc4 arrives for testing, packing dozens of fixes. Drivers make up roughly half of the changes, so expect smoother hardware support soon.
stories.why: Keeps your peripherals from silently failing after updates.

stories.headline: USB GPU fits on a single chip
stories.body: **Graphics on a stick:** Hackaday details a DIY USB GPU built on one chip, targeting pure graphics generation instead of repurposed compute. It shows you can offload rendering without a full GPU board.
stories.why: Offers a low‑cost path for niche visual output in embedded projects.

stories.headline: Sulphur‑3 hits over a hundred‑thousand downloads
stories.body: **Model hype, real numbers:** Hugging Face reports Sulphur‑3 has been downloaded 133,732 times and earned 815 likes. The traction signals strong community interest in its capabilities.
stories.why: Popular models often get better community support and faster bug fixes.

quick_hits.text: **Rust Minecraft:** arnis library creates high‑detail real‑world locations inside Minecraft.
**Rust DB rewrite:** pgrust claims performance beating PostgreSQL and ClickHouse.
**App Store guard:** compliance playbook lists 124 rejection patterns and 112 deadlines.
**Image‑text model:** SenseNova‑Loop‑9B logged 2,036 downloads and 599 likes.
**Port zero oddity:** about 0.25% of hosts still use TCP port zero.

brief.sign_off: Catch you tomorrow, and keep hacking.

highlights.title: Kernel prepatch 7.4-rc4
highlights.summary: Linux kernel 7.4‑rc4 is out for testing, featuring many small fixes with drivers comprising roughly half of the changes.
highlights.detail: Linus Torvalds noted the release is large, with updates across GPU, networking, USB, IIO, NVMe, and sound subsystems, indicating broad hardware support improvements ahead of the final 7.4 launch.

related.title: Three new stable kernels for Tuesday

highlights.title: Show HN: I built a game where you are an LLM's subagent
highlights.summary: A Hacker News post showcases a game where the player acts as a sub‑agent of a large language model.
highlights.detail: The project lets users interact with an LLM indirectly by issuing commands that the model executes, turning the LLM into a collaborative partner rather than a direct chatbot.

highlights.title: louis-e/arnis
highlights.summary: The arnis Rust library generates high‑detail real‑world locations inside Minecraft.
highlights.detail: By mapping geographic data to Minecraft coordinates, arnis lets users recreate precise terrain features, useful for educational or creative projects.

highlights.title: malisper/pgrust
highlights.summary: The pgrust project rewrites PostgreSQL in Rust and claims performance exceeding both PostgreSQL and ClickHouse.
highlights.detail: Leveraging Rust’s safety and concurrency features, pgrust aims to provide a faster, memory‑safe database engine, though benchmark details are not included in the brief.

highlights.title: mjmirza/app-store-compliance
highlights.summary: A compliance playbook and pre‑submission guard for App Store and Google Play includes 124 documented rejection patterns and 112 tracked regulatory deadlines.
highlights.detail: The repository also provides a privacy manifest, Data Safety checks, and a skill designed for AI coding agents to automate compliance verification. It covers EU AI Act, DSA, COPPA, and age‑related laws, helping developers avoid common submission rejections.

items.title: I Heard There Was a Secret Port…
items.summary: A study found that about 0.25% of hosts use TCP port zero, despite the protocol allowing 65,536 ports.
items.detail: Port zero is rarely utilized in practice, and the finding underscores how a small fraction of network devices deviate from typical port usage patterns.
